problem:
Harbour Energy's monthly direct debit collections are due on a day when the creditor PSP and the debtor PSP are both open, but the clearing and settlement mechanism is closed. The billing team asks why the collections cannot simply be submitted and settled anyway, since both banks are working. The answer is that the clearing system is the infrastructure between the banks: it routes the collections from the creditor PSP to the debtor PSP and settles the interbank positions. When it is closed, the banks can accept instructions and prepare files, but the interbank movement cannot happen, and a collection that depends on that movement cannot settle on the planned date.

The distinction matters because the customer experience is misleading. The creditor PSP can accept the file, the creditor can see it as submitted, and the debtor's bank can see the collection as expected, yet no funds move. If the platform reports the collection as settled because it was accepted, the creditor's cash forecast is wrong, the debtor may be debited on a different day from the one promised, and a return or refund that depends on settlement timing is calculated against the wrong date.

Harbour Energy and its PSP need a design that distinguishes PSP availability from infrastructure availability, holds collections that cannot settle, and recalculates the due and settlement dates explicitly when the clearing system is closed, rather than letting the platform imply a settlement that never happened.
solution:
Make infrastructure availability a first-class check, separate from PSP availability. Before a collection is submitted, the platform checks the clearing and settlement mechanism's calendar for the planned settlement date, and if the system is closed, the collection enters a pending-settlement state with a revised settlement date and a revised debit date. The revised dates are calculated against the governing calendars, and the creditor and the debtor are told the revised dates, so no one plans cash against a settlement that will not happen.

Keep the states honest throughout. A collection that is accepted by the creditor PSP is not settled until the clearing system confirms settlement, and the status shown to the creditor, the debtor and Operations must say so. The ledger must not show an interbank settlement that has not occurred, and any customer debit that depends on the clearing settlement must wait for the settlement confirmation or be clearly marked as provisional.

Build the recovery into the design. On reopening, the held collections are submitted in a controlled order, reconciled against the clearing settlement report, and any missing item is escalated before the next cycle. Return and reversal windows are calculated from the actual settlement date, not the planned one. Report monthly on collections held for infrastructure closures, their value and their revised dates, so the business can see how often the constraint bites and whether the billing calendar should be planned around it.

decision.question: You are the business analyst for Meridian Bank's clearing operations. Harbour Energy's collections are due on a day when both PSPs are open but the clearing system is closed. The billing team wants the collections submitted and reported as settled anyway. The operations director asks for your recommendation.

options.label: A
options.detail: Debit the debtors directly without the clearing system and settle the interbank positions later.

options.label: B
options.detail: Hold the collections in a pending-settlement state, recalculate the settlement and debit dates, tell the creditor and debtor the revised dates, and submit when the clearing system reopens.

options.label: C
options.detail: Submit the collections as planned and report them as settled, since both PSPs are open.

options.label: D
options.detail: Cancel all collections for the month and ask customers to pay by another method.

decisionRationale: Option B is correct because PSP availability is not infrastructure availability: the clearing system must route and settle the collections, so they must be held, recalculated and communicated honestly. Option C reports a settlement that never happened and corrupts the cash forecast. Option D cancels a month of collections for a one-day closure. Option A bypasses the clearing system and breaks the interbank settlement model.

steps.title: Generates the collection file for the planned due date
Checks the clearing system calendar and finds it closed on the planned settlement date
Holds the collections in a pending-settlement state with a revised settlement date
Tells the creditor the revised settlement and debit dates
Submits the collections when the clearing system reopens
Routes the collections and settles the interbank positions
Debits the debtor account on the revised due date
Reconciles the held collections against the settlement report

happy: The creditor PSP checks the clearing calendar before submission, finds the closure, holds the collections with a revised settlement and debit date, and tells the creditor and the debtor the revised dates. When the clearing system reopens, the collections are submitted, routed, settled and debited on the revised dates, and the settlement reconciles cleanly.

negative.title: PSPs open but clearing closed
negative.detail: The planned settlement date is a clearing closure day. Hold the collection in a pending-settlement state, recalculate the dates, tell the creditor and debtor, and do not report it as settled.

negative.title: Closure extended after scheduling
negative.detail: The clearing system announces an extended closure after collections were rescheduled. Recheck every held collection against the revised calendar, adjust the dates again, and notify the affected parties of the new dates.

negative.title: Return window miscalculated
negative.detail: A return is assessed against the planned settlement date instead of the actual one. Calculate the window from the actual settlement date, and escalate any return that falls outside it for a decision rather than applying it automatically.

negative.title: Collection lost in the held queue
negative.detail: A held collection is not submitted when the clearing system reopens. Reconcile the held population against the settlement report on reopening, and investigate any item that is missing from the report before the next cycle.

technical: Model infrastructure availability as a calendar service separate from PSP availability, with the clearing system's open and closed days versioned and effective-dated. Model the collection state machine with an explicit pending-settlement state that is distinct from accepted and settled, and never let a transition to settled happen without a clearing settlement confirmation. Record the planned date, the revised date and the closure reason for every held collection. Use correlation IDs to link the held collection, its resubmission, the settlement report and the ledger entry. Reconcile the held population against the settlement report automatically on reopening, and alert on any item missing from the report. Calculate return and reversal windows from the actual settlement timestamp stored in the record.

accounting: Collections accepted while the clearing system is closed must not be assumed settled, so they are held in a pending-settlement state and the ledger shows no interbank settlement until the clearing system reopens and the settlement is confirmed. Any customer account debit that depends on the clearing settlement must wait for the settlement confirmation, or be clearly marked as provisional. Operations works from a clearing-closure worklist that lists every held collection with its revised settlement date, and Finance reconciles the held population against the clearing system's settlement report on reopening. A collection that misses its due date because of a closure is reported to the creditor with the revised date, and the customer is told the revised debit date where the debit itself moves.

questions.explanation: The clearing system routes collections between PSPs and settles the interbank positions. When it is closed, that movement cannot happen even though both banks are open.
options: The banks can settle directly without it
The interbank movement and settlement cannot happen, so the collection cannot settle on the planned date
questions.question: What happens when the clearing system is closed but both PSPs are open?

questions.explanation: Acceptance by a PSP and settlement through the clearing system are different states. Reporting a held collection as settled misstates the cash position and the return and refund timing.
options: Because acceptance and settlement are different states, and the cash forecast and return timing depend on the real settlement date
questions.question: Why must a held collection not be reported as settled?

questions.explanation: The revised dates are the true dates. The customer and the creditor must be told them, so nobody plans against a date that will not happen.
options: State the revised settlement and debit dates to the creditor and the debtor
Keep the original dates to avoid confusion

options: They do not depend on dates

options: Submit a day early without checking

Submit on the planned date anyway
